title: Intrinsic spectral structure of bipartite nonlocal magic resource
authors: Xiao Huang, Guanhua Chen, Yao Yao
abstract: Bipartite nonlocal magic resource (BNMR) quantifies the irreducible nonstabilizerness residing in bipartite entanglement, yet its evaluation is intractable due to the full Hilbert space optimization. Here, we introduce a canonical encoding framework that exactly confines the BNMR of an arbitrary bipartite pure state within a minimal encoding core. This dimension reduction proves that pure-state BNMR is an intrinsic function of the nonzero Schmidt spectrum, extending its invariance from local unitary transformations to local isometries. Leveraging this spectral link, we derive the leading quadratic response of BNMR under spectral perturbations around its zeros. We apply this quadratic response to Haar-random states, deriving and numerically validating the BNMR profile: its distribution is sharply localized at the symmetric bipartition and exponentially suppressed toward asymmetric cuts, in stark contrast to the broadening Page curve of entanglement. Finally, we provide a closed-form expression for the BNMR of Schmidt rank-2 states, uncovering a hierarchy collapse in generalized GHZ states where bipartite and global nonlocal magic resources coincide exactly.
summary: The paper develops a novel, tractable measure called the Bipartite Nonlocal Magic Resource (BNMR) to quantify irreducible nonstabilizerness in bipartite entanglement. By mapping states to a minimal spectral core, the authors prove that BNMR depends only on the Schmidt spectrum, leading to predictions about its distribution for random states and revealing deep structural relationships between global and local quantum resources.
main_problem: The primary challenge is evaluating the Bipartite Nonlocal Magic Resource (BNMR), a measure of irreducible nonstabilizerness in bipartite entanglement, which is computationally intractable due to full Hilbert space optimization.
main_result: The BNMR is shown to be an intrinsic function solely of the nonzero Schmidt spectrum, leading to sharp localization at symmetric bipartitions for random states and revealing a hierarchy collapse in GHZ states where global and local resources coincide.
method: The authors introduce a canonical encoding framework that reduces the state's complexity by mapping it to a minimal core defined by its Schmidt spectrum. They then derive the quadratic response of BNMR under spectral perturbations around zero.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on arbitrary pure bipartite quantum states $|\Psiangle_{AB}$ in a many-body system, particularly examining Haar-random states and generalized GHZ states across various bipartitions.
key_observables: Bipartite Nonlocal Magic Resource (BNMR), Schmidt spectrum ($\lambda$), Global Nonlocal Magic Resource ($M_{	ext{NL}}$), and the quadratic response of BNMR to spectral perturbations.
important_parameters: Schmidt rank ($r$), system dimensions ($d=2$), bipartition asymmetry ($\gamma = r/R$), and perturbation magnitude ($\|\eta\|^2$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that BNMR is an intrinsic, compact measure invariant under local stabilizer operations, allowing for dimension reduction to a minimal encoding core.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the canonical encoding process, showing how complex states reduce to a minimal core. They also compare the calculated quadratic response of BNMR for Haar-random states against theoretical bounds and show the end-to-end encoding structure for GHZ states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the intractability of BNMR, then introducing the canonical encoding to establish its spectral dependence (Proposition 1). It derives the perturbative scaling law (Proposition 2), applies this to random and specific states (Haar-random, rank-2), and concludes by analyzing special cases like GHZ states to show resource collapse.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful new diagnostic tool for quantifying nonlocal quantum correlations beyond standard entanglement measures. The spectral link established between BNMR and the Schmidt spectrum offers a highly structured theoretical framework applicable across various quantum many-body systems.
